cells.rationale: The additive migration carries subtle identity, FTS-preservation, and read-only-boundary invariants across multiple storage surfaces.
Atomic claims, fencing, stale leases, and idempotent completion form a concurrency-critical correctness protocol.
Filesystem-database crash reconciliation, symlink handling, digest verification, and private permissions create concrete correctness and security invariants.
This public admission contract spans many command surfaces and must preserve subtle durability and idempotency guarantees.
Worker cancellation and shutdown races combine with fenced completion and sensitive-output controls in a cross-cutting correctness-critical implementation.
Sensitivity-before-rendering is a security invariant while many-to-many filtering must preserve exact FTS ranking and deduplication semantics.
Installer ownership, singleton lifecycle, foreign-service protection, and private logging create a security-shaped multi-surface rollout.
